method: Curated paraphrases of Microsoft Learn documentation; setting GUIDs identify references, not guaranteed hardware applicability. Runtime AC/DC values and permitted choices are read locally from Windows.

settings.summary: Minimum processor performance target, expressed as a percentage of maximum processor performance.
settings.caution: May interact with hardware-managed performance and silicon-vendor tuning; does not guarantee a fixed clock rate.

settings.summary: Upper bound for the processor performance target, as a percentage of maximum processor performance.
settings.caution: Changing it can reduce peak CPU capability. Firmware, thermal constraints, and the processor's power model still apply.

settings.summary: Controls how the processor selects performance above its nominal level, where supported.
settings.caution: The meaning of aggressive/enabled varies by ACPI, CPPC/PEP, and autonomous processor modes. Follow the platform vendor's tuning guidance.

settings.summary: Idle time in seconds before Windows attempts automatic system sleep.
settings.caution: 0 disables idle-triggered sleep. Available sleep states must be checked separately with powercfg /a.

settings.summary: Selects whether Windows may use hybrid sleep when the platform supports it.
settings.caution: Modern Standby systems and other platforms might not support the corresponding sleep state.

settings.summary: Controls availability of legacy ACPI S1/S2/S3 standby states in the power plan.
settings.caution: Does not add firmware support for unavailable sleep states. Modern Standby is different from legacy S3.

settings.summary: Determines whether application system-required requests can prevent idle-triggered automatic sleep.
settings.caution: Ignoring a valid power request can interrupt running activities. Examine powercfg /requests first.

settings.summary: Time in seconds before Windows turns off the display after user inactivity.
settings.caution: 0 disables the display idle timeout. Lock-screen or managed policy settings can affect actual behavior.

settings.summary: Disk idle timeout; predominantly useful for devices that can spin down or enter supported idle modes.
settings.caution: Microsoft states this idle policy is not used on Modern Standby Windows clients; applicability also varies by storage hardware.

settings.summary: Controls USB selective suspend policy for idle USB devices and hub ports.
settings.caution: Microsoft generally recommends retaining selective suspend to conserve energy. Device drivers determine the actual behavior.

settings.summary: PCI Express link-state power-management preference, from off to moderate or maximum savings.
settings.caution: PCIe device, root-port, firmware and platform support determine which link states are usable.

settings.summary: Power-saving preference for the wireless adapter. Compatibility and operational behavior depend on the adapter driver and access point.
settings.caution: Microsoft recommends consulting the wireless adapter manufacturer before choosing stronger 802.11 power-saving modes.

settings.summary: Defines the action taken when a dedicated sleep button is pressed.
settings.caution: Only applicable where the system exposes a corresponding button and action.

categories.name: CPU & performance
categories.summary: Performance states, boosting and processor-idle policies; silicon-vendor tuning matters.

categories.name: Sleep & hibernation
categories.summary: Sleep entry, wake timers, hibernation and app power requests. Verify supported states separately.

categories.name: Display & graphics
categories.summary: Display inactivity, brightness and video-related energy choices, where registered.

categories.name: Storage & disks
categories.summary: Media idle policies; do not assume legacy HDD settings govern NVMe or Modern Standby.

categories.name: USB & peripherals
categories.summary: Port and device idle/suspend policies. Drivers may implement additional independent controls.

categories.name: PCI Express
categories.summary: Link power-management preferences; actual capabilities depend on the platform and devices.

categories.name: Network & connectivity
categories.summary: Wireless and network energy preferences and wake capabilities. Wake settings also exist outside power plans.

categories.name: Battery
categories.summary: Battery-related thresholds and responses, if registered by the platform.

categories.name: Power buttons & lid
categories.summary: Lid, system power and sleep button actions; availability depends on the hardware.

categories.name: Media & playback
categories.summary: Power policies for media playback/sharing. Actual values come from Windows.

categories.name: General system
categories.summary: Global power-plan settings not covered by a device-specific subgroup.

categories.name: Other settings
categories.summary: Registered settings without a verified category match. No functional assumptions are made.

deviceClasses.summary: USB hubs and controllers may suspend ports independently. Wake and runtime-idle support are driver-dependent.
Network wake permissions differ from Wi-Fi link-power policies. Consult adapter and driver properties.
Bluetooth runtime power and wake capabilities depend on the radio, host controller and driver.
Storage idle behavior differs among HDD, SSD and Modern Standby configurations.
Display power policies differ from graphics-driver power management. Consult the corresponding adapter or monitor driver.
Battery reporting is platform-dependent; a battery policy does not imply every battery metric is exposed.
HID devices may use selective suspend. Wake eligibility is determined separately by driver and firmware.

general.name: Sleep study
general.summary: Modern Standby diagnostic report, where supported.

general.name: Energy analysis
general.summary: Power efficiency and device warnings from the Windows power diagnostics utility.

general.name: Sleep states
general.summary: Lists actual supported and unavailable sleep states and reasons.

general.name: Power requests
general.summary: Lists active system/display/awaymode power requests that may prevent sleep.
